first.rationale: Two metrics (activation, onboarding completion) are down this quarter and both have durable prior evidence (memory_31, memory_86) that reducing signup friction lifts activation and completion — this directly targets the observed regressions with a well-supported lever. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure, but that memory only validates price-sensitive SMB acquisition/revenue lift, not long-term qualified revenue or margin sustainability, and matching a competitor's aggressive pricing risks a race-to-the-bottom that could degrade customer quality and retention — a downstream value risk worth flagging before committing our single experiment slot to it. I want to verify the original promotional_pricing record to check whether retention/LTV or margin effects were measured (not just acquisition), and verify the onboarding simplification record to confirm the lift was durable and not a novelty effect, before running a guarded onboarding-simplification test this week. Given one shot and conflicting pressures, a small guarded test preserves optionality to address pricing pressure next cycle once we know the true tradeoffs.
